A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Appendices A–C match apart from a spelling correction; v3 adds Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and CelebA experiments comparing geodesic and Euclidean distance variability across 30 training seeds, with results in Figure 7 and Table 1.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 results in Figure 7 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Both versions use pullback geometry, cubic-spline energy minimization and ensembles of eight decoders. Appendix D newly documents architectures and perceptual-loss use, but does not establish a revision to the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 5 adds Fashion-MNIST and full CIFAR10 training and evaluation alongside the retained three-class MNIST and CelebA experiments. This substantially broadens image coverage to clothing and general objects, using both existing model families.

E2.justification: Euclidean distance remains the comparator to geodesic distance throughout. The added datasets use the same comparison; newly discussed relative-representation methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce configurations including a CIFAR10 M-flow decoder with 55 million parameters and 22 RQS knots. The shared 100-pair evaluation and coefficient-of-variation metric remain unchanged. Newly documented settings for retained experiments do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends robustness-to-retraining evidence to Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10, testing distance stability under random initialization in the existing injective and relaxed-injectivity settings. It repeats the same analysis without introducing new ablations, stressors or sensitivity sweeps.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 30 training seeds, per-pair coefficients of variation and one-sided Student's t-tests. v3 clarifies the notation and adds results using the same statistical reporting practice, without changing run counts or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 t-statistics of -16.75 and -42.83, respectively, both with reported p-values of 1.00. Figure 7 adds their distributions showing lower geodesic variability. The retained MNIST and CelebA statistics remain -8.64 and -22.33. These additions substantially expand the empirical results without demonstrating same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Assumptions A1–A4, the main definitions and theorems, Proposition 4.8, and the mathematical material in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The revised coefficient-of-variation notation does not alter its definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about identifiable geometric relationships under mild assumptions and post-hoc applicability. The introduction's updated experimental model count reflects additional supporting evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly distinguishes asymptotic identifiability from practical finite-data stability. Section 6 adds an interpretation connecting generator transformations to equivariance and explaining independence from disentanglement assumptions. Section 7's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix D supplies detailed architectures, parameter counts, perceptual-loss use and optimizer information absent from v1. Table 2 specifies geodesic initialization, 10 spline polynomials, 256 discretization points, 4096 maximum steps, learning rate 0.01 and stopping settings. This substantially improves implementation documentation; the repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds discussion of Higgins et al. (2018), Wang et al. (2021) and Zhu et al. (2021). It revises the relative-representations comparison to describe cosine similarity and Yu et al. (2024)'s geodesic proxies. Dataset and implementation citations are also added, while the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 locally expands experimental explanations and related work, adds an experimental-details appendix, and edits capitalization, grammar and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most theoretical exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 expands from two adjacent plots to a labeled four-panel grid. Table 1 gains two dataset columns, Table 2 is added, and Figure 5 moves between columns. Other figures retain their content; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 offers broader empirical validation, substantially clearer implementation documentation in Appendix D, and more precise research positioning. These provide useful incremental gains. Statistical interpretation remains unresolved: both versions report p-values of 1.00 in Table 1 while claiming strong statistical support in the prose.
